articles.title: Police Nab Two Notorious Criminals in ‘Half-Encounter’, Recover Looted Anti-Riot Gun
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh – Action has intensified after the September 26 riots in Bareilly. In a dramatic police operation near Bandiya Canal in CBganj, two criminals involved in looting a police anti-riot gun during the clashes were arrested following an encounter.

body.html:
Bareilly, Uttar Pradesh – Action has intensified after the September 26 riots in Bareilly. In a dramatic police operation near Bandiya Canal in CBganj, two criminals involved in looting a police anti-riot gun during the clashes were arrested following an encounter.

Police shot both accused, Idrees and Iqbal, in the legs, forcing them to surrender. They were later admitted to the district hospital. The stolen anti-riot gun, along with two pistols, cartridges, mobile phones, and a bike, was recovered from their possession.

According to police, Idrees, a resident of Islamnagar Pankhakheda (Madanpur PS, Shahjahanpur), has 20 cases against him, including robbery, dacoity, theft, and gangsterism. His accomplice Iqbal, from Garhi in the same police station area, faces 17 criminal cases. Both were described as “notorious criminals.”

The arrests come after violent clashes broke out on September 26 when a mob allegedly mobilised at the call of Maulana Tauqeer Raza attempted to enter Islamia Ground forcibly. Police were pelted with stones and attacked with gunfire at around ten locations. A police wireless set and anti-riot gun were looted in the chaos.

So far, ten FIRs have been registered at Kotwali, Baradari, Premnagar, Kila, and Cantt police stations, naming 126 people including Tauqeer Raza, along with 3,225 unidentified accused. Police have arrested 81 rioters, of whom 72 have been sent to jail. Among those jailed are Nadeem, Anees Sakailani, and Farhat, along with several IMC leaders.

Authorities have said strict action will continue against those involved in the violence.

articles.title: Mother and Lover Arrested for Brutal Assault on 10-Year-Old Boy in Meerut
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: MEERUT, UTTAR PRADESH: In a shocking incident that has sent shockwaves across Meerut, a 32-year-old woman and her paramour have been arrested for brutally assaulting her 10-year-old son after he caught them in a compromising position.

body.html:
MEERUT, UTTAR PRADESH: In a shocking incident that has sent shockwaves across Meerut, a 32-year-old woman and her paramour have been arrested for brutally assaulting her 10-year-old son after he caught them in a compromising position.

The incident occurred on Monday when the child returned home from school and found his mother with their neighbour, identified as Rajesh, in an objectionable position. When the boy threatened to inform his father, Sanjay, about what he had witnessed, the mother—allegedly at the instigation of her lover—subjected him to a horrific assault.

According to police reports, the enraged woman first beat the child and then inserted a nail polish bottle and a broomstick into his private parts. The boy's screams alerted neighbours, who broke down the door and rescued him.

Critical Condition
The child was rushed to the district hospital in critical condition. Medical reports indicate he has sustained serious injuries, including chemical burns from the nail polish and internal damage from the broomstick. He has undergone surgery and is currently admitted in the ICU under constant medical supervision.

Illicit Relationship
According to police investigations, the woman had developed an illicit relationship with Rajesh after they became friends on Instagram. Her husband, Sanjay, who works as a salesman for a private firm, remained away from home most of the time, during which the relationship deepened.

During interrogation, the accused woman confessed that Rajesh had instigated her to "teach the child a lesson" after the boy threatened to expose their affair.

Father Seeks Justice
A distraught Sanjay reached the SSP office with his two children, demanding justice. "I go out to earn money so that the children are happy, but what has happened to my son? I only want justice," he said in a broken voice, adding that his wife was obsessed with living with her lover and had been torturing the child.

Legal Action
The Nauchandi police have registered a case against both accused under Sections 5 and 6 of the POCSO Act, Sections 323 (assault) and 506 (criminal intimidation) of the Indian Penal Code, and provisions of the Domestic Violence Act. Both the mother and Rajesh were arrested overnight and are in police custody. Police are currently examining Rajesh's call details as part of their investigation.

articles.title: Viral Video of Language Clash in Bengaluru Sparks Debate
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bengaluru – A 25-second video showing a heated argument between two women over language use in a public place has gone viral on social media, reigniting debate over the Kannada–Hindi divide in Karnataka’s capital.

body.html:
Bengaluru – A 25-second video showing a heated argument between two women over language use in a public place has gone viral on social media, reigniting debate over the Kannada–Hindi divide in Karnataka’s capital.

The video, reportedly recorded near a ticket counter, captures a woman in a burqa insisting on speaking in Hindi while another woman in a saree demands that she use Kannada instead. The confrontation quickly escalates, with both women raising their voices.

While the exact cause of the altercation remains unclear, the intensity of the exchange has resonated with many Kannadigas who feel that the Kannada language is being marginalised in public spaces.

Reactions online have been sharply divided. Some social media users expressed anger at what they see as a growing disregard for the state’s official language, while others stressed the need for mutual respect and linguistic harmony in a diverse city like Bengaluru.

The incident has once again brought to the fore long-standing debates around linguistic identity, cultural preservation, and inclusivity in one of India’s most cosmopolitan cities.

articles.title: Engineer Ends Life in Bilaspur After Betrayal in Love, Suicide Note Mentions Woman
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh) – A 30-year-old engineer, identified as Gaurav Savanni, ended his life by jumping in front of a train in the Civil Lines police station area on Saturday evening (27.09.2025).

body.html:
Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh) – A 30-year-old engineer, identified as Gaurav Savanni, ended his life by jumping in front of a train in the Civil Lines police station area on Saturday evening (27.09.2025). Police said he had been under severe mental stress after being accused of rape by a woman with whom he had been in a relationship.

Gaurav, son of retired food inspector Ashok Savanni and a resident of Saket Apartments near Agrasen Chowk, had earlier worked at a private institute in Delhi. While in Delhi, he developed a relationship with a woman who later filed a rape complaint against him. Following this, he was arrested and sent to jail. He was released on bail just 15 days ago and had since been staying with his family in Bilaspur.

According to police, a suicide note was found written on his mobile phone, which also mentioned the woman’s name. His family discovered the note after he went missing on Saturday evening. Later that night, his body was recovered from the Uslapur railway track.

Police have seized the mobile phone and registered a case. The body was sent for post-mortem on Sunday. Investigations are underway.

articles.title: Greater Noida Horror: Man Kills Wife, 6-Year-Old Brother-in-Law with Stone, Then Hangs Himself
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Greater Noida – In a shocking incident in Roza Jalalpur under Bisrakh police station, a 22-year-old man brutally killed his wife and six-year-old brother-in-law with a stone before hanging himself on Monday evening.

body.html:
Greater Noida – In a shocking incident in Roza Jalalpur under Bisrakh police station, a 22-year-old man brutally killed his wife and six-year-old brother-in-law with a stone before hanging himself on Monday evening.

Police identified the accused as Pappu Lal, a resident of Gajraula, Pilibhit. He had been living at his in-laws’ house for the past ten days. On the day of the incident, his father-in-law and mother-in-law were at work, while Pappu, his wife Jaswanti (21), and her younger brother Tej Prakash (6) were at home.

Around 4:30 p.m., after an argument, Pappu attacked Jaswanti with a stone, killing her on the spot. When Tej Prakash witnessed the assault and raised an alarm, he too was fatally attacked. Pappu then locked himself in a room and hanged himself from a ceiling fan.

Preliminary investigation suggests Pappu had been mentally unstable and under severe stress in recent days. Forensic teams and senior officers inspected the scene, and all three bodies were sent for post-mortem.

The incident has shocked the local community, especially since Pappu had been married only four months ago.

DCP Central Noida Shakti Mohan Awasthi confirmed the sequence of events and said a detailed investigation is underway.
